why: A `%{` after code on its line is a line comment, not a block comment's start (MATLAB doc 'Add Comments to Code': the markers must appear alone on their lines), so the script `setupS` assigns `missingQ` on its next line, and once `main` runs it (MATLAB doc 'Scripts vs. Functions': a script runs in its caller's workspace) `missingQ(2)` may index that variable: a dormant row, never a live one (project rule; matlab-dormant.test.ts 'MATLAB script workspaces: a name a script its scope ran makes is a variable, kept dormant'). This guards the script-workspace pass, which parses the script again and must read it as the extractor does (step 12), in LF and in CRLF (the step).
